history.summary: DUPLICATE FLAG: seq 2477 is the same temple as seq 1149 (id belur-math-howrah), already in the dataset. Recorded again here as required. Headquarters of the Ramakrishna Math and Ramakrishna Mission, founded by Swami Vivekananda, chief disciple of Ramakrishna Paramahamsa. Land purchased 4 March 1897; holy relics of Ramakrishna installed 9 December 1898. The main temple fuses Hindu, Islamic, Christian and Buddhist art and motifs as a symbol of the unity of all religions. The campus holds temples to Ramakrishna, Sarada Devi and Swami Vivekananda, a museum, library and the Samadhi Enclosure. NOT A CONVENTIONAL HINDU TEMPLE - a monastic headquarters and spiritual centre of the Ramakrishna Movement (rooted in Hindu Vedanta tradition); keep-or-drop decision needed. CSV town 'Howrah' corrected to Belur.

name: Belur Math
town_description: Belur is a riverside town in Howrah district, West Bengal, on the west bank of the Hooghly river opposite Kolkata. Known worldwide as the site of Belur Math, it is a residential and industrial suburb of the Greater Kolkata region.

travel.airport: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport, Kolkata (~17 km)
travel.railway: Howrah station ~7 km; suburban EMU trains to Belur and Belur Math stations on the Howrah-Bandel line
travel.road: Belur Math Road off G.T. Road; buses (routes 51, 54, 56) from Howrah; ferry across the Hooghly from Dakshineswar/Howrah to Belur Ghat.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Durga Puja is a major draw. Sundays and holidays are busiest.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Morning 6:30 AM-11:30 AM; evening 4:00 PM-9:00 PM (April-September) or 3:30 PM-8:30 PM (October-March), with a mid-day closure. Entry free; modest dress expected; museum has separate hours and is closed Mondays (verify).
